source: 'Caros Ledge UI System.dc.html' p3 (#p3, Regulation detail), 'sticky index' comment block: outer `position:sticky;top:0;background:#FAFAF8;padding:6px 0` wrapping an inner pill-group `display:flex;align-items:center;gap:4px;background:#fff;border:1px solid rgba(0,0,0,.12);border-radius:8px;padding:4px;font-size:12.5px`, whose current-section item is a FILLED pill (`padding:6px 12px;border-radius:6px;background:#5A5552;color:#fff;font-weight:700`, text "S1 Summary", no separator dot) and whose other items are plain links (`padding:6px 12px;border-radius:6px;font-weight:600;color:#5A6B67`, e.g. "S2 Obligations"). README §0.5 says only 'sticky section index (S1 · S2 · S3 …)', which is README's own shorthand notation for the artboard's numbered links, not a literal middot-separated instruction.
notes: REAL STRUCTURAL DIVERGENCE, not a harness artefact: the artboard's index is a bordered PILL GROUP (white background, 1px border, 8px radius, 4px padding) with the current section rendered as a filled dark pill and the others as plain 6px-radius links inside that group — SectionIndex.tsx instead renders a bare flex row of underline-free links separated by a literal '·' character, with no pill container and no current-section highlight at all (no scroll-spy / active-link logic exists in the component). Per the operator's framing, the artboard wins over README's own shorthand notation.

The label text itself differs too: the artboard's links read "S1 Summary" / "S2 Obligations" (numeral and label separated by a space only); the built component renders "S1 · Summary" (DetailShell.tsx: `S${i + 1} · ${s.label}`).
